doc.title: Bob Magnusson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Latin music and touring South America with Sarah Vaughan
summary: He loves Latin music and toured South America with Vaughan. He describes Argentine tango bass playing with the bow and rhythm on the off beats.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Do you ever feel compelled to try to learn music that’s coming into the area from those populations?

Well I’ve always liked Latin music. I don’t know, if you said oh that’s a merengue or, I don’t know all the technical terms. And I’ve even played with some Latin guys, in more kind of a jazz-Latin sort of context, and I’ll say that to some of them and they says — just play how you feel and stuff. And I’ve of course picked up some of the sense of it and I got to tour South America a couple of times with Sarah which was a great experience. Argentina and Brazil and all over South America. And so I got to hear a lot of it live,

some of the real authentic music, the tango in Argentina, and the bass players play with the bow down there. Marvelous. I mean, and burning, swinging stuff. So that’s always been a music that I’ve loved. And maybe sometime I’ll have the time to really learn more about it.
Some of that stuff is really odd. I mean the bass never seems to fall—

Right, yeah. They play on the ands of two and the downs of four. They’re not playing on the ones and threes like most of our Western music is. So it’s really interesting music. And I’ve learned to feel some of it from that place. And I like it very much.
